The driver's own arrival message at 14:06 puts him "at the side road" and the rider replied at 14:07 "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you"; the driver's closest approach over the whole wait was 40 m and his stationary position 14:05:55–14:09:55 was 179 m from the pin, so he never came to the pickup point the rider was at.

There is no record in the file of any driver tap of the "$5 Waiting Time Fee" button or of any waiting fee charged — only the $6.61 cancellation fee — and the driver cancelled at 14:09:55 rather than completing a trip, so no waiting-fee item can stand under NS-6 either (amount claimed: $5.00, F7).

Because the arrival-tap condition (NS-1(i)/(ii)) is not satisfied on the system records, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2; the amount is the cancellation fee recorded in F4/F7, and NS-7 makes it payable as a Ryde voucher.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against us is F6: the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for 3 min 40 s after his 14:06:15 "I'm Here" tap, and F2 shows 5 min 55 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation — with the data-layer 200 m radius the driver will argue NS-1(iii) is satisfied and the $6.61 stands.

The arrival was a driver tap, not a platform auto-confirmation: the timeline separately records the platform arrival log at 14:03:20 [F5] and the driver's own "I'm Here" tap at 14:06:15 [F6], so NS-1(i) is satisfied on the driver_tap branch [NS-1].

NS-1(ii) requires that GPS placed the driver at the pick-up location at the moment of the tap. The trace marks this ✓: at the tap the driver was 178 m from the pickup point, inside the data-layer 200 m arrival radius, with a closest approach of 40 m at 14:03:50 [F6][F1][NS-1]. Nothing in NS-1 fixes the measurement at the pin rather than the pick-up location area, and the rider's argument that the pin/entrance coordinates differ from the driver's 179 m stationary position is not established anywhere in the fact table [F3][F10][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes after the tap until cancellation. The GPS trace covers the wait without a break [F2][F6][NS-1], and after the 14:06:15 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (220 s > 180 s) until he cancelled at 14:09:55 [F6][F4][NS-1]. The stationary block of 4 min 0 s at 14:05:55–14:09:55 [F3] is consistent with that wait, and F2 shows 5 min 55 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation [F2][NS-1]. All three NS-1 conditions therefore hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands, and NS-2 (which only applies where any of (i)–(iii) fails) is not triggered [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's post-trip statement that he was parked at the pickup and waited more than 3 minutes [F13] is consistent with the system records rather than displacing them [F3][F6][NS-1]. The rider's message "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" [F10] shows she did not reach the car the driver announced "at the side road" [F9], but the record does not show the driver left the pick-up area, and the fee's conditions are met on the records [F9][F10][NS-1].

No separate waiting-fee item exists in this case: F7 lists only the $6.61 cancellation fee and no $5.00 waiting fee was charged [F7][NS-6]. NS-7's 30-day window and voucher form govern a refund that does not arise here, since the charge is valid [F4][F7][NS-7]. what_would_change: Had the driver confirmed arrival more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 while the record shows he was 178 m from the pickup point at that moment, so the NS-1(i)/(ii) requirement that the arrival tap coincide with GPS showing the driver at the pickup point is not met on the record as given.

The driver's own arrival message at 14:06 puts him "at the side road" and the rider replied at 14:07 "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you"; the driver's closest approach over the whole wait was 40 m and his stationary position 14:05:55–14:09:55 was 179 m from the pin, so he never came to the pickup point the rider was at.

There is no record in the file of any driver tap of the "$5 Waiting Time Fee" button or of any waiting fee charged — only the $6.61 cancellation fee — and the driver cancelled at 14:09:55 rather than completing a trip, so no waiting-fee item can stand under NS-6 either (amount claimed: $5.00, F7).

Because the arrival-tap condition (NS-1(i)/(ii)) is not satisfied on the system records, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2; the amount is the cancellation fee recorded in F4/F7, and NS-7 makes it payable as a Ryde voucher.

The driver's post-trip statement that he was "parked at the pickup, a short walk from the entrance" is contradicted by the GPS record placing him 179 m from the pickup point, so the system record prevails.

The rider has a clean 90-day no-show record (0 upheld) and the driver already has 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days plus an arrival tap made 178 m from the pin, which warrants sending the driver's account to Ryde review in addition to the refund.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against us is F6: the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup point for 3 min 40 s after his 14:06:15 "I'm Here" tap, and F2 shows 5 min 55 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation — with the data-layer 200 m radius the driver will argue NS-1(iii) is satisfied and the $6.61 stands.

The driver's statement F13 asserts he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes, and the timeline F5 shows he cancelled 6 min 35 s after the platform-recorded arrival at 14:03:20 — the judge may treat the wait length as effectively conceded.

The 178 m distance at the tap (F6) is inside the 200 m data-layer radius used for NS-1(ii), so our argument turns on the narrow reading of "at the pick-up location" (the pin/entrance the rider was told to meet at) rather than on a clear numeric breach.

The complaint says the driver "was not at the entrance where the pin was", but nothing in the fact table establishes where exactly the pin/entrance coordinates are relative to the driver's 179 m stationary position (F3), so the entrance-versus-side-road mismatch is partly rider-supplied narrative (F10).

claims.assertion: The pickup arrival is a driver tap: the driver pressed "I'm Here" at 14:06:15, and the case record shows the platform's own arrival log at 14:03:20 separately (F6, F5).
At the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was 178 m from the pickup point, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius (F6), and his closest approach was 40 m at 14:03:50 (F1).

The driver then waited continuously at the pickup: stationary 14:05:55–14:09:55 (4 min 0 s) at 179 m from the pickup (F3), and within 200 m from 14:03:20 until the cancellation at 14:09:55 — 5 min 55 s cumulative (F2, F4) — so NS-1(iii)'s 'more than 3 minutes' is met.
The ride was cancelled only at 14:09:55, i.e. 3 min 40 s after the tap and 6 min 35 s after the recorded arrival, and the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F4, F5, F6, F7) therefore satisfies NS-1.

The rider could not find the driver despite the driver announcing his exact position: driver at 14:06 "I'm here, silver Toyota Altis, at the side road." and rider at 14:07 "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" — the rider's own message shows the rider was not at the car, and the rider still did not board over the following ~2 min 55 s (F9, F10, F4).
The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F12), so the timing of the wait period (F6, F3) can be determined from the record and no G12 gap arises.
The ride was a RydeX trip, so the cancellation policy applies to it and $6.61 is the published cancellation fee, of which $4.50 is payable to the driver (F4, F7).
The driver's statement that he parked at the pickup and waited more than 3 minutes (F13) is consistent with, not contradicted by, the GPS and timeline records (F3, F6).

weaknesses: The driver's very own record shows 178–179 m from the pickup point at the tap and while stationary (F6, F3); the rider will argue the pin was at the entrance and the car was on a side road, so the driver was not at the designated spot even though he was inside the 200 m radius the policy works with.

The rider's complaint and her message "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" (F10) can be read as the driver being in the wrong place; the driver's chat "at the side road" (F9) arguably concedes he was not at the entrance.

The driver's profile shows 1 no-show dispute upheld in the last 90 days (F18); if the judge were to treat this case as established misconduct, the rider will use F18 to invite a flag_account (RD-6), so we must keep the finding at NS-1 satisfied and no refund.

points.response: Conceded on form: the record shows a driver tap at 14:06:15 with a separate platform arrival log at 14:03:20 (F6, F5); my case does not dispute that a tap was made, only that the tap does not satisfy NS-1(ii).

The 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, not a policy clause, and NS-1(ii) requires GPS to show the driver "at the pick-up location"; the driver's own message places him "at the side road" (F9) while the rider was at the entrance (F10), and his stationary position was 179 m from the pin (F3) — inside the radius but not at the pickup location.

The 4 min 0 s stationary block ran 14:05:55–14:09:55 (F3), which starts AFTER his own message of 14:06 admitting he was on a side road (F9) and after the rider told him at 14:07 she could not see him (F10); a wait spent in the wrong place where the rider cannot reach the car is not waiting "for the rider to arrive at the pick-up point" under NS-1(iii).

The fee's validity is not measured by elapsed time alone; NS-1 requires all three conditions, and because (ii) is not met on the system records the $6.61 must be refunded under NS-2 despite the 3 min 40 s wait (F6, F4).

The rider's message is evidence of her being at the entrance as instructed (F10), and she was never told to walk to "the side road" before the car appeared there; nothing in the record shows the driver moved the 179 m to the entrance during the ~2 min 55 s he remained stationary at his own position (F3).

I do not rely on any gap; the chat record is complete and timestamped (F12), which is precisely why the 179 m stationary position and the 178 m tap distance are provable on the system records (F3, F6).
The $6.61 being the published fee and $4.50 going to the driver only matters if NS-1 is satisfied; since the arrival-tap condition fails, NS-2 controls and the whole $6.61 is refundable (F4, F7).

"A short walk from the entrance" concedes he was not at the entrance; the GPS places him parked 179 m away for the whole block (F3) and 178 m away at the tap (F6), so the statement is contradicted by the system record, which prevails under NS-1.

NS-1(ii) is met on the system records: the "I'm Here" tap at 14:06:15 placed the driver 178 m from the pickup point (F6), within the 200 m arrival radius, and nothing in the policy text of NS-1 fixes the measurement at the pin rather than the pick-up location area.

The rider's own message "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" at 14:07 (F10) shows the rider had not come to the car the driver had announced "at the side road" (F9), and the driver still waited until 14:09:55 (F4) — closeness of approach is only an element of NS-1(ii), which F6 satisfies; the 40 m approach at 14:03:50 was his closest point before repositioning (F1).
Conceded as to the item: no waiting fee of $5.00 is on the record here — F7 lists only the $6.61 cancellation fee — so there is no separate waiting-fee sum for us to defend under NS-6.

The refund premise fails because NS-1's (i)-(iii) are satisfied on the records: tap made (F6), position inside the 200 m radius at the tap (F6), and continued waiting past 3 minutes — 3 min 40 s after the tap and 5 min 55 s cumulative within 200 m (F6, F2, F3) — so the $6.61 in F4/F7 stands and NS-2 is not triggered.

F13 is a location claim, not a distance claim: the system record confirms he was at the pickup area (inside 200 m at the tap, stationary 179 m from the pin, F6, F3, F2), and the record the rider relies on is the very record that satisfies NS-1, so nothing is displaced.

NS-2 permits `flag_account` only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, or where the fee must be refunded (F6 shows 178 m, inside the 200 m radius); the rider's own history shows a dispute filed in the last 90 days (F17) with 0 upheld, and the driver's 4.86 rating across 312 trips in 90 d (F18) does not support an abuse finding, and profile facts cannot decide the case.

Answering their reliance on NS-7: NS-7 governs the timing and voucher form of a fee the rider has been charged, and it does not create a refund where the charge is valid under NS-1; the 30-day window is met but irrelevant to the outcome.
